svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Transcription (in the nucleus): RNA polymerase separates the two DNA strands and moves along the template strand."], [0.8, "Free RNA nucleotides pair with the template bases (A\u2013U, T\u2013A, C\u2013G, G\u2013C). RNA polymerase joins them: the mRNA grows 5\u2032\u21923\u2032."], [6, "The mRNA leaves the nucleus through a nuclear pore and goes to a ribosome in the cytoplasm."], [8, "Translation: the mRNA binds to the small subunit. The start codon AUG sits in the P site with tRNA carrying methionine (anticodon UAC)."], [9.5, "A tRNA with the complementary anticodon enters the A site. A peptide bond forms, so the chain moves onto the tRNA in the A site."], [11.7, "The ribosome moves one codon along the mRNA (5\u2032\u21923\u2032). The empty tRNA leaves from the E site; the A site is free again."], [13, "The cycle repeats: tRNA in, peptide bond, ribosome moves on. The polypeptide grows one amino acid at a time."], [20, "Stop codon (UAA) in the A site: no tRNA matches. A release factor binds and the polypeptide is released."], [21.6, "The ribosome subunits separate. The polypeptide (Met\u2013Ala\u2013Lys\u2013Trp\u2026) folds into its protein shape."]]
svg.title: Protein synthesis: transcription and translation
svg.desc: Transcription in the nucleus: RNA polymerase copies the template strand of a gene into mRNA, which leaves through a nuclear pore. Translation at a ribosome: tRNAs with anticodons bring amino acids to the codons of the mRNA, peptide bonds join them, and the ribosome moves along to the stop codon.
svg.text: Not to scale. Only a short gene is shown; DNA is drawn unwound (it re-forms its double helix behind the polymerase).

g.data-info: The DNA strand with the same base sequence as the mRNA (but T instead of U). It is not used as the template.
The DNA strand that RNA polymerase reads. The mRNA is complementary to it.
Messenger RNA: a copy of the gene made of RNA nucleotides (ribose, and uracil instead of thymine). It carries the code to a ribosome.
Enzyme that binds at the promoter, separates the DNA strands and joins RNA nucleotides into mRNA, in the 5′→3′ direction.
Double membrane round the nucleus. Transcription happens inside; translation happens outside, in the cytoplasm.
Gap in the nuclear envelope through which mRNA leaves the nucleus.

svg.text: 2. Translation: at a ribosome in the cytoplasm

g.data-info: Transfer RNA: carries a specific amino acid at its 3′ end and has an anticodon that pairs with the codon.
Carried by a tRNA. Each tRNA carries one particular amino acid, matching its anticodon.
Made of rRNA and protein: a large and a small subunit, with three tRNA binding sites, E, P and A. It moves along the mRNA one codon at a time.
Messenger RNA: a copy of the gene made of RNA nucleotides (ribose, and uracil instead of thymine). It carries the code to a ribosome.
UAA, UAG or UGA: no tRNA matches it. A release factor binds and the polypeptide is released.
A triplet of three bases on the mRNA that codes for one amino acid (or start/stop). 64 codons; the code is degenerate and universal.
Transfer RNA: carries a specific amino acid at its 3′ end and has an anticodon that pairs with the codon.
Carried by a tRNA. Each tRNA carries one particular amino acid, matching its anticodon.
Amino acids joined by peptide bonds (condensation reactions, catalysed by the ribosome). The polypeptide then folds into a protein.
